IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL ORIGINAL JURISDICTION
TRANSFER PETITION (CRIMINAL)  NO.535/2026
X                                             Petitioner(s)
                          VERSUS
UNION TERRITORY OF JAMMU AND KASHMIR & ANR.   Respondent(s)
O R D E R
1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. Through this transfer petition, the petitioner, a
victim of crime, seeks transfer of Sessions Challan
No.50/2025 titled “U.T. through PS Baramulla versus
Towseef Ahmad Shagoo” pending in the Court of third
Additional Sessions Judge, Baramulla, Kashmir to a
competent court in Delhi.
3. The case of the petitioner is that she was duped into
a relationship and exploited thereafter under a false
promise of marriage. According to her, offences were
committed within the territorial limits of Delhi, but
1

--- Page 246 ---
under a wrong advice she lodged a First Information
Report at Baramulla, Kashmir.  She also claims that
the investigation was not conducted properly, though a
charge-sheet  has  been  submitted  and  a  trial  is
pending.  It is also her case that she had applied to
the  Sessions  Court  for  further  investigation.
According to her, the application seeking further
investigation is pending.
4. In the context of the above submissions, we have
perused the record carefully.  A perusal of the record
would reveal that according to her own case she had
travelled to Baramulla, Kashmir with the accused and
there she was portrayed as a wife.
5. In such circumstances, it cannot be said that the
Court at Baramulla completely lacks jurisdiction.
6. At this stage, our attention was invited to ground (q)
in the transfer petition where she has expressed
apprehension  regarding  threat  to  her  life.  The
respondent denies existence of any such threat to her
life. 
7. Having regard to the place where the Sessions Trial is
proceeding as also that the petitioner happens to be a
domicile  of  Delhi,  in  our  view,  it  would  be
2

--- Page 247 ---
appropriate  and  necessary  to  secure  the  ends  of
justice that the subject proceedings be transferred to
an area where such threat perception may not be there.
After considering the submissions, we are of the view
that  ends  of  justice  would  be  served  if  the
proceedings are transferred from Baramulla to Jammu.  
8. Accordingly, this transfer petition is partly allowed.
The  subject  proceedings  i.e.  Sessions  Challan
No.50/2025 titled “U.T. through PS Baramulla versus
Towseef Ahmad Shagoo” pending in the Court of third
Additional Sessions Judge, Baramulla, Kashmir shall
stand transferred to the Court of Sessions at Jammu.
The transferor Court shall forthwith transmit the
records to the Sessions Judge (Jammu). Upon receipt of
the records, the Sessions Judge (Jammu) shall either
hold the trial himself or nominate an Additional
Sessions Judge for conducting the trial.  
9. We make it clear that we have not expressed any
opinion on the merits of any application which may be
pending  in  the  Trial  Court  for  seeking  further
investigation of the matter and, therefore, the said
application, if it has not yet been decided, shall be
addressed and decided on its own merits in accordance
with law by the Court to which the trial stands
3

--- Page 248 ---
transferred.
10. As soon as the records of Sessions Case are received
by the Transferee Court, the Transferee Court shall
inform the parties concerned including the petitioner
regarding the next date in the proceeding so that
parties including the petitioner can engage counsel of
their choice.
11. Pending applications, if any, shall stand disposed of.

………………………………………………………J.
                           [VIJAY BISHNOI]

JULY 28, 2026

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.           OF 2026
(@SLP(CRL.) NO.10967 OF 2026)
KRISHAN CHANDER MALIK ..... APPELLANT(S)
              VERSUS
SIDHESHWAR SINGH @ SIDHESHWAR DALAL  ..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Heard.
2. Leave granted.
3. Since no orders adverse to the interest of the respondent is
being passed while disposing of this appeal as the present appeal,
if kept pending, the appellant, who is an accused and convicted
under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (NI Act)
would  protract  the  proceedings  and  thwart  the  same,  we  are
disposing of this appeal.
4. The appellant/accused, filed an appeal against an order of
conviction and sentence of one year simple imprisonment along with
fine of Rs.3,51,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 138
of NI Act, sought for production of additional evidence in the
appeal. Since the said application was rejected by the Appellate
Court, appellant filed a revision petition before the High Court,
wherein the interim stay of the proceedings before the Appellate
Court, was sought for, was not granted. Revision petition was
filed. No notice has been issued in the revision petition and the
High Court has also directed the Sessions Court not to adjourn the
matter simply because of the pendency of the present petition.
1

--- Page 257 ---
Essentially no fault can be laid at the doors of the High Court. Be
that as it may, fact remains no orders have been passed in the
revision petition. Hence, this appeal.
5. The said order of adjourning the matter having been challenged,
this Court by order dated 04.06.2026 directed the appellant to
deposit a sum of Rs.2 lakhs in the Registry of this Court and said
amount was ordered to be kept in a Fixed Deposit in a nationalised
bank initially for a period of three months and directed the
Registry to keep the FD alive by renewing, if required. In the
meanwhile, the further proceedings of the Appellate Court has been
stayed.
6. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant and
on perusal of the records, we notice from the office report that
amount as ordered, has been deposited and the same has been kept in
a short term Fixed Deposit by the Registry.
7.The issue relating to rejection of application for additional
evidence, has to be adjudicated by the High Court. We are of the
view that the ends of justice would be met if the stay of the
proceedings before the Sessions Court, as ordered by this Court, is
continued till disposal of the revision petition and accordingly,
it is made absolute. We request the High Court to expeditiously
dispose of the revision petition as it stands on a very limited
issue, expeditiously and preferably within six weeks from today.
8. The amount in deposit along with accrued interest, shall be
transmitted by the Registry of this Court to the Additional
Sessions Judge, Rohtak, forthwith and the Sessions Judge on receipt
of the orders, that would be passed in the revision petition by the
jurisdictional  High  Court,  Sessions  Court  shall  proceed  to
adjudicate the appeal on merits expeditiously and dispose of the
same within an outer limit of two months from the date of receipt
of the order from the High Court. The amount which is transmitted
2

--- Page 258 ---
to the Sessions Court, shall be paid to the successful party and
the Appellate Court would be at liberty to pass necessary orders in
that regard.
9. It is made clear that no prayer for adjournment shall be
entertained by the Sessions Court or the High Court, as the case
may be, and in the event of such a request being made, the advocate
can be discharged and an amicus curiae can be appointed from the
jurisdictional Bar or a panel counsel from the legal services
authority so as to conclude the proceedings as ordered hereinabove.
10. We also make it clear that without being influenced by any
observations made under the impugned order including this order,
the Courts below shall dispose of the matters on merits and in
accordance with law. Both Courts would be at liberty to mulct the
parties with costs as it deems fit on the principle of ‘cause
should follow cause’.
11. We hope and trust that both parties and their respective
learned counsels would extend full cooperation with the courts in
disposing the matter(s) and would not take any steps to delay or
protract the proceedings. Accordingly, the appeal stands disposed
of.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
..................J.
(ARAVIND KUMAR)
..................J.
(VIPUL M. PANCHOLI)
New Delhi;
July 22, 2026.

the intervener(s). The stand of the State Government that they will
abide by the directions of this Court is appreciated but a candid
and categorical stand could properly help the Court from resolving
a long pending controversy. For, in matters of this nature, the
State  is  the  authority  finally  responsible  for  preserving
archeologically important structures. 
7. The parties, including interveners, are given two weeks’ time
from today to file their objections/suggestions before the Chief
Secretary (Mining), State of Rajasthan and the State Government
would examine every aspect, file its categorical view on the area
needed to be prohibited from activity including blasting, and the
area in which blasting activity can go forward. 
8. The Chief Secretary is given liberty to decide whether an

PRASHANT GIRISHBHAI YOGANANDI APPELLANT
                        VERSUS
STATE OF GUJARAT          RESPONDENT
O R D E R
1. Heard. 
2. Leave granted.
3. Appellant  while  working  as  Sales  Manager  in
Axis  Bank  is  said  to  have  facilitated  opening  of
accounts and assisted the prime accused in operation
of opening ‘mule accounts’ which was used in cyber
fraud transaction.
4. This Court by interim order dated 25.05.2026
has  granted  an  interim  protection  in  favour  of
1

--- Page 272 ---
appellant subject to appellant cooperating with the
investigation.
5. Ms. Swati Ghildiyal, learned AOR appearing for
the respondent – State would fairly submit that the
appellant  has  appeared  before  the  Investigating
Officer. However, she  would hasten to  add that in
order  to  trace  the  money  which  has  gone  to  the
accounts, she would require further time to make her
submissions.
6. Having regard to the fact that entire case of the
prosecution is based on the statements of accounts of
the  bank,  we  are  of  the  considered  view  that
custodial  interrogation  of  appellant  would  not  be
warranted.  The  alleged  antecedent  relates  to  the
same transaction, namely, multiple FIRs having been
registered  against  the  appellant  in  respect  of  the
same  offence  in  various  other  States  as  such  it
cannot  be  prima  facie construed  as  a  criminal
antecedents. In that view of the matter, the appeal is
allowed and the appellant is ordered to be released
2

--- Page 273 ---
on anticipatory bail on such terms and conditions as
the  Investigating  Officer  deems  fit  to  impose
including the condition of directing the appellant to
appear  before  the  Investigating  Officer  on  every
Monday between 11:00 A.M to 02:00 P .M. till filing of
the chargesheet and continue to appear before the
trial  court  on  all  dates  of  hearing  except  when
exempted. In the event of any conditions imposed by
the Investigating Officer or by this Court is violated,
the State or the complainant would be at liberty to
move the jurisdictional Court for cancellation of bail. 
7. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  stand
disposed of.

Petition(s) for Special Leave to Appeal (C)  No(s).  30672/2024
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated 04-10-2024
in CRP No. 2620/2024 passed by the High Court for The State of
Telangana at Hyderabad]
CHERUKURI SANJAY                                   Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
CH SATYA                                           Respondent(s)
(IA No. 37027/2025 - CONDONATION OF DELAY IN FILING THE SPARE 
COPIES)
 
Date : 30-07-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K.V. VISWANATHAN
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ARUN PALLI
For Petitioner(s) :  
                   Mr. Sanjay Cherukuri, in-person
                    
For Respondent(s) : 
                   Ms. Mary Mitzy, Adv.
                   Mr. B Ravikiran Singh, Adv.
                   Mr. Oleander D Singh, Adv.
                   Mr. Pratham Sadh, Adv.
                   Mr. Tushar, Adv.
                   Mr. Shivam Tomar, Adv.
                   Mr. Ashutosh Jha, AOR
                                      
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay is condoned in filing the spare copies.
2. The  present  Special  Leave  Petition  calls  in
question the correctness of the order dated 4 th October,
2024 in Civil Revision Petition No.2620 of 2024 passed by
1

--- Page 294 ---
the High Court for the State of Telangana at Hyderabad.
By the said order, the High Court confirmed the order of
the VI Additional District and Sessions Judge-cum-Family
Court, Ranga Reddy District Kukatpally in IA No.764 of
2024 in FCOP No.2986 of 2018.  The Trial Court had, by
its order, rejected the petition filed by the petitioner
herein  under Section  45 of  the Indian  Evidence Act
seeking a direction to the respondent to give her thumb
impression and for forwarding the same to the Forensic
Science  Laboratory.   This  was  to  substantiate  the
original Settlement Agreement purportedly entered into by
the petitioner and the respondent on 14th April, 2015.
3. The High Court held that the petitioner has other
ways of proving the so-called Settlement Agreement.
4. We heard Mr. Sanjay Cherukuri, petitioner in person
and Ms. Mary Mitzy, learned counsel appearing for the
respondent.
5. When we asked learned counsel for the respondent as
to what the stand of the respondent is with regard to the
thumb impression on the purported Settlement Agreement,
learned counsel drew attention to para 4 (xiv) which is
part of the counter affidavit filed by the respondent.
Para 4(xiv) of the counter affidavit filed in this Court
which reads as under:
“xiv) The Respondent filed a Counter to the IA
2

--- Page 295 ---
stating that no probative or evidentiary value
can be given to Annexure R-1 MOU which is a
fabricated document.  The text in the said blank
papers were inserted at a later stage.  A plain
reading of text inserted in the said impugned MOU
filed by the petitioner makes it very clear the
said text was inserted in the absence of the
Respondent herein.  Without admitting anything,
even for a moment assuming it to be existing, no
Indian woman would make such revelations as shown
in the inserted text in front of other male
members who were shown as witnesses to the said
document.”
6. In view of this averment in the counter affidavit,
the application filed by the petitioner for referring the
matter  to  the  Forensic  Science  Laboratory  becomes
unnecessary. The stand of the respondent is that the text
in the blank papers was inserted at a later stage.  The
petitioner disputes this position and submits that it was
a validly arrived at settlement.  The respondent has a
case that from reading the terms of the settlement, it
would be clear that no woman would make such revelations
as written in the said text.
7. These are the matters to be considered at the
trial.  In view of the stand of the respondent that the
text of the document was subsequently inserted and only
on  that  account  it  is  a  fabricated  document,  the
3

--- Page 296 ---
application  of  the  petitioner  to  refer  the  thumb
impression to the Forensic Science Laboratory does not
arise.
8. The Special Leave Petition is disposed of in the
above terms.
9. Pending application, if any, shall stand disposed
of.
(ANITA MALHOTRA)                         (NIKITA SINGH)
     DEPUTY REGISTRAR                          COURT MASTER

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL ORIGINAL JURISDICTION
ARBITRATION PETITION NO. 25 OF 2026
AHMED SHAMMA PETITIONER
VERSUS
UNIVERSAL INDUSTRIAL PLANTS 
MFG. CO. (P) LTD.
RESPONDENT
O R D E R
1. This petition under Section 11(6) of the Arbitration and
Conciliation Act, 1996 (“the Act”) seeks the appointment of a
sole  arbitrator  to  adjudicate  disputes  arising  from  the
Contracts  dated  10.11.2018,  27.09.2020,  and  28.07.2023
executed between the predecessor-in-interest of the Petitioner
and the Respondent.
2. The Respondent is an Indian private limited company, engaged
in the manufacture and supply of oxygen/nitrogen plants and
allied equipment. The Petitioner’s father entered into a
Purchase  Contract  dated  10.11.2018  with  the  Respondent,
whereby  the  Respondent  would  supply  a  customised
oxygen/nitrogen plant. Two further contracts dated 27.09.2020
and 28.07.2023 were also executed, seemingly towards the same
end. It is submitted that advance payments of approximately
USD 176,690 (INR 1.7 crores) were made to the Respondent.
3. It appears from the pleadings that dispute arose between the
parties  on  account  of  alleged  delays  in  initiation  of
development/manufacture of the plant, which led the Petitioner
to terminate the contracts and demand a refund of its advance
1

--- Page 310 ---
payment. The Respondent, on the other hand, declined such
liability, citing manufacturing and storage costs already
incurred in anticipation of fulfilling the order. In these
circumstances, disputes arose between the parties in relation
to the aforesaid Contracts. It is noteworthy that Clause (iii)
of the ‘Standard Terms and Conditions of Supply’ attached to
the  contract  dated  28.07.2023  provides  for  reference  of
disputes between the parties to a Sole Arbitrator  to be
appointed by the Respondent, with the seat at New Delhi.
4. The Respondent initially sent an Arbitration Notice dated
28.01.2025, followed by a petition under Section 11(6) before
the Delhi High Court seeking appointment of an Arbitrator.
Meanwhile, the Petitioner, being ordinarily resident in Egypt,
has filed the instant petition in light of Section 11(9) of
the Act.
5. We have heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and perused
the material placed on record. None appears for the Respondent
despite service of notice having been attempted. However,
since the Respondent has itself invoked the arbitration clause
and initiated proceedings under Section 11 of the Act in
respect of the very same disputes, the existence of a valid
and binding arbitration agreement between the parties is not
in dispute.
6. Keeping in view the facts and circumstances recorded above and
Clause (iii) of the ‘Standard Terms and Conditions of Supply’
2

--- Page 311 ---
in Contract dated 28.07.2023, we deem it just and proper to
allow the instant Arbitration Petition and appoint Justice
Rakesh Kumar Jain, former Judge, Punjab & Haryana High Court
and former Member, National Company Law Appellate Tribunal, as
the Sole Arbitrator to resolve the disputes between the
parties.  The  seat  and  venue  of  arbitration  shall,  in
accordance with the arbitration agreement, be New Delhi.
7. The Arbitrator shall have the liberty to fix his/her own
remuneration/fees. Ordered accordingly.
8. Pending  interlocutory  applications,  if  any,  also  stand
disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL ORIGINAL JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL No.     OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRIMINAL) No.8565/2026)
MUNSHIRAM BHALADAR ..... APPELLANT(S)
              VERSUS
THE STATE OF RAJASTHAN & ANR.  ..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the parties.
3. This appeal takes exception to the order dated 07.02.2026,
passed by the High Court of Rajasthan Bench at Jaipur (briefly the
‘High Court’ hereinafter) rejecting the prayer for regular bail of
the appellant.
4. Appellant is an accused in FIR No.125/2025, registered at
Police  Station  Kotwali  Sikar,  District  Sikar,  under  Sections
318(2), 316(2) and 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (for
short, ‘BNS’).
5. This Court by Order dated 13.05.2026, issued notice pursuant
to which State has filed counter affidavit.
1

--- Page 322 ---
6. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is a
land broker which is his only source of livelihood. He submits that
appellant has not prepared any fabricated or forged document as
alleged. He has not committed any fraudulent act to defraud the
informant of his money. He is in custody since 26.07.2025.
7. Per contra learned State counsel referring to the averments
made in the counter affidavit submits that it would be wrong to
simply describe the appellant as a land broker. He was actively
involved in the commission of the offence. She submits that trial
has commenced in this case whereafter 5 prosecution witnesses have
been examined out of 27. At this stage, it would not be just and
proper to enlarge the appellant on bail.
8. We have considered the rival submissions and perused the
materials on record. On due consideration, we are of the opinion
that a case for grant of bail is made out. The charges against the
appellant are Magistrate trialble. The trial has commenced but only
5 out of 27 prosecution witnesses have been examined. An early
conclusion of the trial does not appear a possibility. In the
meanwhile, appellant has already undergone custody for more than 1
year.
9. That being the position, we set aside the impugned order of
the High Court dated 07.02.2026 and direct that the appellant shall
be produced before the concerned Magistrate within a maximum period
of 7 days from today who shall enlarge the appellant on bail on
such terms and conditions as may be deemed appropriate.
2

--- Page 323 ---
10. Criminal Appeal is accordingly allowed.
11. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
INHERENT JURISDICTION
SUO MOTO CONTEMPT PETITION(CRIMINAL)  No(s).  1/2026
IN RE: VIBHAS KUMAR JHA, A PRACTICING ADVOCATE IN ROHINI DISTRICT
COURTS, DELHI
O R D E R
1. The  respondent-contemnor  (Vibhas  Kumar  Jha),  an  advocate
practising before the Rohini District Courts, Delhi, is present in
person along with Mr. Kunal, his learned counsel. Some other
respectable members of the Tis Hazari Bar are also present. All of
them have, in one voice, expressed regret on behalf of the
respondent-contemnor  for  his  contemptuous  actions.  They  have
further stated unequivocally that it would be their responsibility
to  ensure  that  the  respondent-contemnor  conducts  himself
respectfully and ethically and does not indulge in the activities
which are ex facie criminal contempt of court.
2. The respondent-contemnor (Vibhas Kumar Jha) has also filed an
unconditional apology by way of an affidavit dated 21.07.2026,
inter-alia,  explaining that at any point of time, he had no
intention  or  motive  to  scandalise  this  Court,  to  lower  the
authority of the Court or to interfere with the administration of
justice.
3. He has placed on record the family circumstances that had
driven him into a state of depression, and it was under the
1

--- Page 330 ---
influence of that disturbed state of mind that the alleged act of
contempt was committed. He has further explained that the post on
social media has neither been re-published, re-posted, nor has he
circulated the same. He has also given an undertaking that he shall
not, directly or indirectly, republish or disseminate the said
offending material or any content thereof, which would amount to
undermining the dignity, authority or majesty of this Court. He has
further stated in the affidavit that all the posts have been
voluntarily removed/deleted from the social media platforms.
4. The affidavit also records an undertaking of respondent-
contemnor to the effect that he shall maintain the highest degree
of  responsibility,  restraint  and  sensitivity  in  all  public
statements, writings and social media activity and shall ensure
that no act of omission on his part undermines or is capable of
being perceived as undermining the dignity, authority or majesty of
this Court.
5. The  respondent-contemnor  has  expressed  his  remorse  and
tendered an unconditional and unqualified apology with a prayer to
take a compassionate and lenient view in the matter.
6. We have heard the respondent-contemnor in person along with
members of the District Bar.  In view of the repentance shown by
the respondent-contemnor and the undertaking given by way of an
affidavit, we are inclined to accept the unconditional apology
tendered by the respondent-contemnor.  Ordered accordingly.
2

7. The contempt proceedings are, consequently, dropped.  Rule
discharged.

2. The petitioner, along with co-accused family members are

can take a considerable amount of time.

after hearing the learned counsel for the parties, we are of the
opinion that the petitioner can be released on bail, and such other
terms  and  conditions  that  the  Additional  Sessions  Judge-04,
(Shahdara), Karkardooma Courts, Delhi  (the jurisdictional court)

ITEM NO.23               COURT NO.11               SECTION IX
               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A
                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
Petition(s) for Special Leave to Appeal (C)  No(s).  22985/2026
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated  07-04-2026
in EPL No. 12766/2025 passed by the High Court of Judicature at
Bombay]
SADANAND SARVANKAR                                 Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
MAHESH BALIRAM SAWANT & ORS.                       Respondent(s)
IA No. 191373/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING C/C OF THE IMPUGNED 
JUDGMENT
IA No. 191379/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.
 
Date : 30-07-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM    HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANOJ MISRA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAY BISHNOI
For Petitioner(s)  Mr. Mukul Rohatgi, Sr. Adv.
                   Mr. Dilip Annasaheb Taur, AOR
                   Mr. Amol V Deshmukh, Adv.
                   
                   
For Respondent(s)  
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The submission on behalf of the petitioner is
that the statutory limitation for presenting the
Election Petition was expiring on 07.01.2025. The
Election  Petition  was  initially  presented  on
04.01.2025, at around 1315 hours. As cash counter
had closed, security deposit of Rs. 2,000/- though
offered was not accepted. Therefore, on 06.01.2025,
the cash deposit of Rs. 2,000/- was made and the
1

--- Page 367 ---
Election Petition was again presented. The election
petitioner presented himself along with his Advocate
on 06.01.2025 and was examined. Receipt of security
deposit was tendered and a note to that effect was
made indicating that all requisite formalities for a
valid presentation were complete. Thereafter, the
petition  was  admitted.  However,  the  returned
candidate  filed  an  application  to  dismiss  the
Election  Petition  on  the  ground  that  security
deposit did not accompany the Election Petition on
04.01.2025 i.e., date of its initial presentation
and, therefore the same was liable to be rejected
under  Section  117  read  with  Section  86  of  the
Representation of the People Act, 1951. The High
Court  accepted  the  submission  on  behalf  of  the
returned  candidate  and  by  the  impugned  order
dismissed the petition.
2. The contention on behalf of the petitioner is
that the petitioner could not make the deposit on
account of the High Court Rules which regulate the
time of deposit and limits it to 12 noon. An
Election Petition can be submitted /presented up to
the last date of limitation, that is up to midnight
of the day on which limitation expires. Here, the
last date of limitation was 7 th and, therefore, it
could have been presented up to 7 th midnight. The
security deposit was made on 6 th, and the Election
2

--- Page 368 ---
Petitioner had appeared before the Registrar and
verified the petition and had submitted the deposit
receipt on 6th. In such circumstances, even assuming
the petition did not accompany the security deposit
on 04.01.2025, the presentation of the petition for
all legal purposes took place on 06.01.2025, within
limitation. Thus, there was no justification to
dismiss  the  Election  Petition  for  failure  to
accompany it with security deposit on date of its
initial presentation.
3. Issue notice, returnable in four weeks.     
(CHETAN ARORA)                                  (SAPNA BANSAL)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        COURT MASTER (NSH)
3

--- Page 369 ---

For Respondent(s)  Mrs. Prerna Dhall, Adv.

     UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Heard Mr. Kaustubh Shukla, learned counsel for the
petitioner and  Mr. Prashant Singh,  learned counsel
appearing for State.

--- Page 406 ---
2
2. The  present  petition  calls  in  question  the
correctness of the order dated  18-03-2026 in MCRC No.
1068/2026 passed by the High Court of Chhattisgarh at
Bilaspur. By the said order, the petitioner has been
denied the benefit of bail in connection with FIR
No.468/2025 registered with Police Station Mohan Nagar,
District  Durg,  Chhattisgarh,  for  the  offences
punishable under Section 20( B) of the Narcotic Drugs
and  Psychotropic  Substances  Act,  1985(for  short,
‘NDPS’).
3. Learned  counsel  for  the  petitioner  submits  that
petitioner has already undergone about ten months and
18 days in custody. Learned counsel submits that even
according to the prosecution the contraband is not
recovered from the petitioner and the case is that on
account of confession of co-accused  Sajid Ali , the
petitioner has been roped in. The allegation is that he
facilitated the contraband at cheaper prices and that
he has also received commission.
4. Learned counsel for the State submits that 08 more
witnesses remained to be examined.
5. Considering the nature of the allegation; the fact
that the petitioner is roped by the confession of the
co-accused  and  the  fact  that  contraband  is  even
according to the prosecution, not recovered from the
petitioner; all this coupled with the fact that the
trial is likely to take time and bearing in mind the

--- Page 407 ---
3
twin condition of Section 37 of NDPS Act, w e are
inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
6. Accordingly, we direct that petitioner shall be
enlarged on bail subject to the satisfaction of the
concerned Trial Court in connection with the aforesaid
FIR and for the offences mentioned hereinabove.
7. The Special Leave Petition is disposed of in the
above terms.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand
disposed of.
(NIRMALA NEGI)                             (MANOJ KUMAR)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                   COURT MASTER (NSH)

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The  present  petition  has  been  filed  by  the
1

--- Page 505 ---
petitioner, being aggrieved by the High Court’s rejection
of the application for condonation of delay.
2. The petitioner’s contention is that she works as a
coolie and did not have sufficient funds to make both ends
meet. Furthermore, she did not have the funds to engage a
lawyer and to pay the court fees.
3. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent has
stated that there is a huge delay of 714 days in the matter
and that the High Court was justified in dismissing the
application for condonation of delay.
4. This Court, after hearing the parties at length, is
of the opinion that keeping in view the fact that the
petitioner lost her husband at young age, works as a
coolie,  has  two  minor  school-going  children,  and  was
unaware of the aspect of limitation in legal proceedings,
the  present  petition  deserves  to  be  allowed  and  is
accordingly allowed.
5. The application for condonation of delay stands
allowed. The High Court shall decide the matter on its
merits without taking into account the issue of limitation,
given the peculiar facts and circumstance of the case.
6. The High Court is requested to decide the matter as
expeditiously as possible at an early date.
7. With  the  above  observation,  the  Special  Leave
petition stands disposed of.

for the offences punishable under Sections
305, 317(4), and 331(4) of the  Bharatiya

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner has
submitted  before  this  Court  that  the
petitioner has been in jail for the last one
year and four months, and that the other co-
accused persons have also been granted bail.
3. On the other hand, learned counsel for
the  respondent-State  of  Jharkhand  has
vehemently opposed the prayer for the grant
of  bail.  She  has  submitted  that  the
petitioner has criminal antecedents.
4. This Court, keeping in view the period
of incarceration of the petitioner and the
fact that the other co-accused persons have
already been granted bail, is of the opinion
that the application for the grant of bail
deserves to be allowed and is, accordingly,
allowed. The petitioner is directed to be
released on bail forthwith, subject to the
usual terms and conditions to be imposed by

                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. Exemption Application is allowed.
3. Leave granted.
4. These appeals have come up today to consider the plea of the
appellants - convicts for suspension of substantive order of
sentence of 10 years of rigorous imprisonment and release on bail,
pending the final disposal of their appeals before this Court.

--- Page 938 ---
2
5. We take notice of the fact that the appellants - convicts were
put to trial in C.C.No.383 of 2021 for the offence punishable under
Sections 8(c) read with 20(b)(ii)(C), 25 and 29(1) of the NDPS Act,
1985, respectively.
6. The contraband involved in the present case is 52 kgs of
Ganja. The appellants were held guilty of the alleged offence by
the Trial Court and were sentenced to undergo a fixed term of 10
years of rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.1,00,000/-.
7. The appellants went in appeal before the High Court. Their
appeals before the High Court came to be dismissed, thereby
affirming the Judgment and Order of conviction passed by the Trial
Court.
8. We take notice of the fact that the appellants have been
convicted and sentenced for a fixed term of 10 years. They have
already undergone more than 5 years by this time.
9. Since we are to look into their appeals on merits and the
appeals are likely to take time before it is taken up for hearing,
we are persuaded to exercise our discretion in favour of the
appellants.
10. We suspend the substantive order of sentence of 10 years and
order that the appellants be released on bail forthwith, if not
required in any other case, subject to terms and conditions that
the Trial Court may deem fit to impose.
11. We make it clear that the appellants shall be released after
the amount of fine of Rs.1,00,000/- each is deposited by them with
the Trial Court.
12. Tag with Criminal Appeal No.878/2026.
 (VISHAL ANAND)                                    (POOJA SHARMA)

expeditiously.
